materials.name: Air Elemental Core
materials.desc: A fist-sized knot of screaming wind that tugs at the vessel walls. The standard keystone for flight, speed and storm enchantments.

materials.name: Stormglass Shard
materials.desc: Sand fused into clouded glass by the vortex's dying lightning; tiny clouds drift inside it. Used to predict and bottle weather.

materials.name: Skyborne Grit
materials.desc: Fine grey dust that refuses to settle and drifts upward if poured. Alchemists fold it into draughts of haste and lightness.

materials.name: Earth Elemental Core
materials.desc: A dense, warm lodestone that grinds softly against itself, like a heartbeat in rock. Keystone for earthen, burrowing and stoneskin magic.

materials.name: Earth Elemental Living Stone
materials.desc: Grey rock veined with slowly shifting mineral threads; it knits cracks in itself over days. Masons prize it for wards and indestructible foundations.

materials.name: Tremor Gravel
materials.desc: Coarse gravel that shivers at the faintest footfall. Scattered in trays, it serves as a tremor-sensing alarm.

materials.name: Fire Elemental Core
materials.desc: A white-hot ember that never dims, straining to leap free and ignite everything. The classic keystone for flame weapons and the only fuel that melts adamantine.

materials.name: Everburning Cinder
materials.desc: A coal-black lump that glows red along its cracks and burns for a year without being consumed. Smiths and lamp-makers pay well.

materials.name: Flame-Walker Ash
materials.desc: Feather-light ash that stays warm to the touch. Rubbed into leathers and salves, it wards off burns.

materials.name: Water Elemental Core
materials.desc: A sphere of impossibly clear water that holds its shape and sloshes with tides of its own. Keystone for water-breathing, swimming and tidal magic.

materials.name: Tidewater Pearl
materials.desc: A blue-green pearl that is always damp and smells of the open sea. Held under the tongue it eases breath in water; jewellers set them into diving charms.

materials.name: Undertow Brine
materials.desc: Heavy, dark saltwater that swirls against the direction you pour it. A base for potions of swimming and brine-curing sea-leathers.

materials.name: Azer Forge-Core
materials.desc: A small bronze-cased ember from an azer's chest, hot enough to soften steel. A cheap substitute for a greater fire core in a forge.

materials.name: Azer Bronze Flesh
materials.desc: Warm, bronze-like skin plates that cool into a naturally tempered alloy. Smiths hammer it into heat-proof fittings.

materials.name: Azer Flame-Hair
materials.desc: Strands that still flicker with little flames. Woven into wicks, they burn for weeks without smoke.

materials.name: Djinni Tempest Core
materials.desc: A crackling sphere of storm-cloud that murmurs in a proud, ancient tongue. The keystone for true flight, storm-calling and fortune-bending magic.

materials.name: Djinni Wishglass Bead
materials.desc: A tear-shaped bead of sky-blue glass, formed from the genie's last exhalation. Said to hold the faint echo of an ungranted wish.

materials.name: Djinni Cloudsilk Hair
materials.desc: Long, nearly weightless strands that drift upward like smoke. Weavers spin them into carpets and cloaks that ride the wind.

materials.name: Efreeti Brazier-Core
materials.desc: A coal the size of a heart, wrapped in a lattice of molten brass. The keystone for mighty flame, plane-walking and forge-magic of the efreet's brass cities.

materials.name: Efreeti Brass Cinders
materials.desc: Glittering brass-flecked ash that clings together like iron filings near a lodestone. The traditional binder for bottles and rings that imprison spirits.

materials.name: Efreeti Ember-Blood
materials.desc: Blood like liquid magma, cooling to a glossy black crust at the edges. Drunk in tiny doses, it wards the body against flame.

materials.name: Dust Mephit Core
materials.desc: A tiny whirl of grit that makes anyone who stares at it yawn. Used in sleep-draughts and blinding powders.

materials.name: Dust Mephit Grit
materials.desc: Stinging, bone-dry dust that clogs eyes instantly. Thieves pack it into eggshell blinding bombs.

materials.name: Ice Mephit Core
materials.desc: A snowflake-shaped mote that frosts the inside of its vessel. Keystone for small frost charms and fog-making trinkets.

materials.name: Ice Mephit Frost Shard
materials.desc: Jagged slivers of blue ice that melt only very slowly. Packed into cold boxes and chilling salves.

materials.name: Magma Mephit Core
materials.desc: A dribbling drop of lava that never cools. A common, cheap fire core that bigger forges burn through by the dozen.

materials.name: Magma Mephit Slag
materials.desc: Glassy black lava rock that stays warm for weeks. Used as a slow-heat stone for crucibles and bedwarmers.

materials.name: Steam Mephit Core
materials.desc: A bead of shimmering vapour that blurs the air around it. Illusionists use it for blur and obscuring charms.

materials.name: Steam Mephit Scald-Drops
materials.desc: Water that keeps boiling in a sealed flask without any heat. A quick way to brew tea, sterilise tools, or scald a foe.

materials.name: Gargoyle Stoneskin
materials.desc: Flexible slate-grey plates that feel like stone but bend like thick leather. Armourers use it for petrification-proof linings and tough bucklers.

materials.name: Gargoyle Talon
materials.desc: A chipped, granite-hard claw. Ground down it makes a potent abrasive; whole, a vicious dagger-point.

materials.name: Gargoyle Heartstone
materials.desc: A cold, egg-shaped stone that looks exactly like ordinary rubble. Enchanters prize it for camouflage and stone-to-flesh work.

materials.name: Invisible Stalker Core
materials.desc: An unseen, cold pressure trapped in the vessel; you only know it is there by the frost on the glass. Keystone for invisibility and unerring tracking magic.

materials.name: Invisible Stalker Clearglass
materials.desc: A pane of utterly transparent crystal that casts no reflection. Lens-makers and illusionists use it for see-through gear and vanishing wards.

materials.name: Magmin Core
materials.desc: A cheerful, sputtering spark that tries to light anything nearby. Cheap forge fuel and the heart of everburning torches.

materials.name: Magmin Lava Crust
materials.desc: Brittle red-black flakes of cooled magma skin. Crushed into tinder powders that ignite at a spark.

materials.name: Salamander Heart
materials.desc: A glowing, fist-sized heart that keeps pumping molten blood long after death. Smiths burn it to reach temperatures that melt adamantine.

materials.name: Salamander Tail
materials.desc: A long coil of heat-scaled muscle that tightens around anything it touches. Rope-makers weave it into fiery bindings and whips.

materials.name: Salamander Scales
materials.desc: Overlapping red-bronze scales that radiate heat. Laid into armour, they turn aside flame.

materials.name: Xorn Gut-Stones
materials.desc: Half-digested gemstones polished smooth inside a xorn's gizzard, each glowing faintly with earth-magic. Jewellers value them as much as the raw gems.

materials.name: Xorn Gizzard
materials.desc: A thick, gravel-lined stomach that phases partly through stone when squeezed. Keystone material for earth-gliding and burrowing magic.

materials.name: Xorn Jaw-Teeth
materials.desc: Blunt, diamond-hard grinding teeth from the crown mouth. Set into picks and drills they chew through rock.

materials.name: Xorn Essence
materials.desc: A slow-turning mote of gravel-light that can sense metal through walls. Used for treasure-finding and stone-passing enchantments.

materials.name: Ghast Stench Gland
materials.desc: A swollen, grey sac that reeks of an opened crypt. Rendered into nauseating smoke bombs and poison bases.

materials.name: Ghast Claw
materials.desc: A yellowed talon slick with a paralytic film strong enough to stiffen even an elf. The poisoner's favourite paralysis source.

materials.name: Ghast Grave-Dust
materials.desc: Grey dust scraped from a ghast's marrow, cold and faintly greasy. A standard reagent for necromantic inks.

materials.name: Ghost Ectoplasm
materials.desc: Pale, glistening mist that half-exists; it slides through the fingers and into the Ethereal if not sealed. Used for etherealness and phasing magic.

materials.name: Ghost Essence
materials.desc: A mournful wisp that shows a fleeting face when it presses against the glass. Keystone for possession, fear and spirit-walking enchantments.

materials.name: Ghost Anchor Keepsake
materials.desc: The small object — a locket, a ring, a letter — that tied the ghost to this world, now cold and heavy with sorrow.

materials.name: Ghoul Claw
materials.desc: A blackened, jagged claw crusted with grave filth and a numbing residue. A standard paralysis ingredient.

materials.name: Ghoul Saliva
materials.desc: Stringy grey drool that numbs the tongue at a touch. Poisoners concentrate it; healers boil it into anaesthetics.

materials.name: Lich Phylactery Shard
materials.desc: A splinter of the vessel that once held a lich's soul, still cold enough to burn. The supreme keystone for soul-binding, deathlessness and necromancy.

materials.name: Lich Essence
materials.desc: A whirling, violet-black spark that whispers formulae in a dead tongue. Keystone for archmage-grade necromancy and counter-magic.

materials.name: Lich Dust
materials.desc: The fine, grey-violet dust a lich's body crumbles into. A potent necromantic reagent that chills the air it is poured through.

materials.name: Lich Finger-Bones
materials.desc: Blackened finger bones rimed with a frost that never melts; a touch leaves skin numb and rigid.

materials.name: Skeleton Bone-Dust
materials.desc: Chalky white powder ground from reanimated bone, still humming faintly with necromantic will. The cheapest undead reagent on any necromancer's shelf.

materials.name: Skeleton Grave-Gear
materials.desc: Corroded weapons and scraps of old armour. Mostly scrap, occasionally something worth cleaning up.

materials.name: Minotaur Skeleton Horn
materials.desc: A massive curved horn, bleached and cracked, still fused with the momentum of a thousand charges. Carved into battering rams and charging charms.

materials.name: Minotaur Skeleton Skull
materials.desc: A bull's skull that seems always to face the nearest exit. Maze-runners hang fragments of it as path-finding talismans.

materials.name: Warhorse Skeleton Hoof
materials.desc: A heavy bone hoof that clatters on its own if dropped. Used in charms of tireless riding and phantom steeds.

materials.name: Warhorse Skeleton Barding
materials.desc: Rusted scraps of cavalry barding that can be restored into decent plates.

materials.name: Mummy Wrappings
materials.desc: Resin-stiff linen bands inked with faded funerary glyphs. Carriers of mummy rot — and prized for curses, wards and preservation magic.

materials.name: Mummy Glare-Eye
materials.desc: A shrivelled eye behind a dried lid that still fixes you with an unsettling stare. Keystone for paralysing fear effects.

materials.name: Mummy Embalming Resin
materials.desc: Dark, aromatic resin that preserves anything it coats against decay. Burns fiercely, like the mummy itself.

materials.name: Mummy Lord Heart
materials.desc: A black, dried heart taken from its canopic jar, beating once a day. The keystone for rejuvenation and deathless magic.

materials.name: Mummy Lord Royal Wrappings
materials.desc: Gold-threaded burial linen dense with priestly curses. Wrapped around a weapon or ward, it carries a pharaoh's doom.

materials.name: Mummy Lord Essence
materials.desc: A dry, spice-scented swirl of dark gold light that commands the dead to kneel. Keystone for great curses and command of undead.

materials.name: Zombie Grave-Flesh
materials.desc: Grey, rubbery dead flesh that twitches when prodded. Revolting but reliable necromantic filler for animation rituals.

materials.name: Zombie Undying Sinew
materials.desc: Tough, cord-like tendons that refuse to stay severed. Stitched into armour straps and charms against being dropped.

materials.name: Ogre Zombie Sinew
materials.desc: Thick, rope-strong tendons from an undead ogre. Bowyers and necromancers both value their brute pull.

materials.name: Shadow Essence
materials.desc: A chill smudge of living darkness that avoids the light inside its vessel. Keystone for stealth, shadow-hiding and darkvision.

materials.name: Umbral Residue
materials.desc: A fine black soot left where a shadow was unmade; it drinks light around it. Rubbed on blades and leathers to kill their gleam.

materials.name: Specter Ectoplasm
materials.desc: Thin, cold vapour that drifts through the walls of an unwarded jar. A weaker cousin of ghost ectoplasm, used for incorporeal charms.

materials.name: Specter Essence
materials.desc: A hollow, hungry wisp that dims any flame near it. Keystone for life-drain and deathly enchantments.

materials.name: Vampire Fang
materials.desc: A long, ivory-white canine that still draws blood toward it. Keystone for life-stealing weapons and hypnotic charms.

materials.name: Vampire Heart-Ash
materials.desc: Silver-grey ash from a staked and burned vampire heart, faintly warm despite the fire being long cold. One of the most potent necromantic reagents known.

materials.name: Vampire Blood
materials.desc: Dark, slow blood that crawls up the inside of the vial toward any living warmth. A dangerous restorative and charm base.

materials.name: Vampire Essence
materials.desc: A crimson mote that shifts between the shapes of bat, wolf and mist. Keystone for domination, charm and shapechanging magic.

materials.name: Vampire Coffin-Earth
materials.desc: Dark soil from a vampire's resting place, cold and faintly damp. Necromancers use it to anchor undead to a place.

materials.name: Vampire Spawn Fang
materials.desc: A sharp, slightly translucent fang from a lesser vampire. Set into daggers that sip blood.

materials.name: Vampire Spawn Blood
materials.desc: Thick, chill blood that clings to walls like the spawn did. A base for regeneration tonics and spider-climb oils.

materials.name: Wight Essence
materials.desc: A cold, spiteful ember of stolen life that makes nearby corpses twitch. Keystone for raising and commanding lesser undead.

materials.name: Wight Barrow-Dust
materials.desc: Heavy grey dust from a wight's crumbling body, smelling of old barrows. A strong life-draining reagent.

materials.name: Wight Ember-Eyes
materials.desc: Withered eyes with a pinprick of cold red light at their centre. They see in utter darkness.

materials.name: Wight Barrow-Blade
materials.desc: An old barrow-king's sword, pitted and cold to hold. Reforged, it takes necrotic enchantments readily.

materials.name: Will-o'-Wisp Lantern-Core
materials.desc: A flickering blue-white spark that winks in and out of sight. Keystone for light, lightning and vanishing-lantern magic.

materials.name: Will-o'-Wisp Marsh-Glow
materials.desc: Pale luminous oil that condenses where a wisp dies; it glows for days and stings with static.

materials.name: Wraith Ectoplasm
materials.desc: Inky, smoke-like ectoplasm that deadens sound around it. Used for incorporeal and wall-passing magic.

materials.name: Wraith Essence
materials.desc: A hateful black flame that pulls at the soul of whoever holds its vessel. Keystone for life-drain weapons and creating spectral servants.

materials.name: Animated Armor Plate
materials.desc: Dented steel plates that still flinch toward blows aimed at the wearer. Armourers rivet them into self-guarding armour.

materials.name: Animated Armor Animus Rune
materials.desc: A small plate etched with a glowing binding rune — the spark that made the suit move. Keystone for minor animation magic.

materials.name: Clay Golem Shem Tablet
materials.desc: A clay tablet stamped with a holy name, the animating word placed in the golem's mouth. Keystone for binding constructs and resisting magic.

materials.name: Clay Golem Clay
materials.desc: Damp, dark clay that swells when it touches acid and leaves wounds that refuse to close. Potters and poisoners both prize it.

materials.name: Flesh Golem Galvanic Core
materials.desc: A jar-like organ of wires and sinew still crackling with the storm that raised it. Keystone for lightning-fed animation and restoration.

materials.name: Flesh Golem Stitched Hide
materials.desc: A patchwork of skins sewn with heavy thread, strangely resistant to blades. Unpleasant but tough leather.

materials.name: Flesh Golem Mismatched Organs
materials.desc: Organs from half a dozen bodies, fused together and faintly humming with current. Alchemists render them into galvanic tonics.

materials.name: Flying Sword Blade
materials.desc: A fine blade that still twitches upward in the hand. Re-hilted, it balances unnaturally well.

materials.name: Flying Sword Hover-Rune
materials.desc: A tiny rune set into the pommel that makes whatever it touches weightless. Used for levitating and returning charms.

materials.name: Homunculus Blood-Drop
materials.desc: A bead of its creator's blood that animated the creature; it still vibrates when its maker is near. Keystone for telepathic links.

materials.name: Homunculus Venom
materials.desc: A drop of clear venom that sends the bitten into a deep, dreamless sleep.

materials.name: Homunculus Wing
materials.desc: A small leathery wing, like a bat's. Used in minor levitation charms.

materials.name: Iron Golem Core
materials.desc: A heavy iron heart inscribed with interlocking wards, glowing like a banked furnace. Keystone for mighty constructs and magic-resistant armour.

materials.name: Iron Golem Vent Slag
materials.desc: Greenish, bubbling slag from the golem's breath-vent; it still weeps toxic vapour. Poisoners and siege-engineers covet it.

materials.name: Iron Golem Plating
materials.desc: Hand-thick iron plates that drink in flame and turn spells aside. Smiths forge them into nearly impervious armour.

materials.name: Rug of Smothering Fibres
materials.desc: Thick, patterned yarn that tightens around anything wrapped in it. Weavers use it for grasping nets and ordinary-looking snares.

materials.name: Rug of Smothering Animus
materials.desc: A knotted sigil woven into the rug's back, the binding that made it strangle. A minor animation keystone.

materials.name: Shield Guardian Amulet Shard
materials.desc: A fragment of the control amulet, still resonating with the guardian's protective bond. Keystone for warding, shielding and bond-magic.

materials.name: Shield Guardian Core
materials.desc: A slowly pulsing stone-and-metal heart that repairs itself in a day. Used in self-repairing wards and guardian constructs.

materials.name: Shield Guardian Spell Cavity
materials.desc: A rune-lined hollow built to hold a single spell until triggered. Crafters use it for spell-storing items.

materials.name: Stone Golem Core
materials.desc: A heavy, rune-cut stone heart that feels magic slide off it. Keystone for stone constructs and spell-resistant wards.

materials.name: Stone Golem Lethargy Stone
materials.desc: Grey stone that makes anyone holding it feel sluggish. Used in enchantments that slow time and foes.

materials.name: Black Pudding Acid
materials.desc: A tar-black, stinking acid that eats metal and wood alike. Alchemists concentrate it into corrosive flasks.

materials.name: Black Pudding Split-Jelly
materials.desc: A still-dividing lump of pudding that swells if fed. Used for regeneration and growth reagents.

materials.name: Gelatinous Cube Gel
materials.desc: Perfectly clear, slightly acidic gel that nearly vanishes in its jar. Base for invisibility and numbing salves.

materials.name: Gelatinous Cube Nucleus
materials.desc: A dense, cloudy lump that coordinates the cube's digestion. Rendered into potent digestive acids.

materials.name: Gelatinous Cube Undigested Hoard
materials.desc: Coins, buckles, bones and weapons suspended in the cube, slowly etching. What's left is often worth a look.

materials.name: Gray Ooze Slime
materials.desc: Wet, stone-coloured slime that corrodes metal. Thieves use it to eat through locks and chains.

materials.name: Gray Ooze Corrosion Salt
materials.desc: A brittle white crust left when the ooze dries. Dissolved in water, it pits metal overnight.

materials.name: Ochre Jelly Acid
materials.desc: Yellow, sticky acid that clings to ceilings. Used in climbing gels and corrosive coatings.

materials.name: Ochre Jelly Budding Mass
materials.desc: A fist-sized lump that tries to split again. Used in minor regeneration and growth reagents.

materials.name: Awakened Shrub Twigs
materials.desc: Springy twigs that rustle when no wind blows. Used in camouflage charms.

materials.name: Awakened Shrub Wakeful Leaf
materials.desc: A leaf that murmurs faintly when held to the ear. Brewed into tea that helps speak with plants.

materials.name: Awakened Tree Sap
materials.desc: Amber sap that warms in the hand and smells of spring. A popular base for healing and growth tonics.

materials.name: Awakened Tree Heartwood
materials.desc: Dense, dark heartwood with faint rings of memory. Carved into staves and druidic foci.

materials.name: Awakened Tree Bark
materials.desc: Thick, gnarled bark; tough but vulnerable to fire. Used in druidic armour.

materials.name: Shambling Mound Vines
materials.desc: Slimy, rope-thick vines that still crackle with absorbed lightning. Woven into storm-charged nets and lightning-feeding charms.

materials.name: Shambling Mound Rot-Heart
materials.desc: A knot of rotting roots at the mound's core, humming with current. Keystone for lightning-fed growth magic.

materials.name: Shrieker Cap
materials.desc: A pale mushroom cap that shrieks when disturbed, even after picking. Used for alarm charms and sonic weapons.

materials.name: Shrieker Spores
materials.desc: Fine spores that hum when they settle. Scattered as alarms around a camp.

materials.name: Treant Heartwood
materials.desc: Ancient, iron-hard heartwood that still slowly grows. The finest staff and bow wood in existence.

materials.name: Treant Sap
materials.desc: Golden, life-giving sap that makes seeds sprout on contact. Potent healing base.

materials.name: Treant Bark
materials.desc: Thick plates of weathered bark tough as stone. Druids craft it into protective armour.

materials.name: Treant Essence
materials.desc: A green, slow-pulsing mote that makes nearby trees sway toward it. Keystone for animating plants and great nature magic.

materials.name: Treant Seed-Acorn
materials.desc: A giant acorn containing the seed of a new treant. Planted in a sacred grove, it may one day awaken.

materials.name: Violet Fungus Tendril
materials.desc: A rubbery purple tendril that rots flesh on contact. Used in necrotic poisons.

materials.name: Violet Fungus Spores
materials.desc: Fine purple spores that cause rotting sores. Used in disease-based curses and poisons.

monsters.name: Air Elemental
monsters.blurb: A howling column of wind; when it breaks apart, the calm eye at its centre can be caught if you are quick.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. The core bucks violently: on a failed check it escapes as a gust that knocks you prone.
Scattered where the funnel collapsed; sift the debris before the next wind buries it.
Must be collected with a lidded jar held upside down.

monsters.name: Earth Elemental
monsters.blurb: A hulking mass of animated bedrock; when it falls, its heart sinks toward the ground unless someone digs it out fast.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. It tries to sink into the floor; stand on stone and you must dig for it.
Only the few chunks still twitching are true living stone; the rest is common rubble.

monsters.name: Fire Elemental
monsters.blurb: A roaring shape of living flame; as it gutters out, the seed that fed it flares one last time.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. Handling it bare-handed deals 2d6 fire damage; tongs or fireproof gloves required.
Pick them from the scorch mark while they still glow; soaked cinders go dead.

monsters.name: Water Elemental
monsters.blurb: A crashing wave with a will; when it bursts, a single lucid droplet and a few pearls remain in the puddle.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. It flows toward the nearest body of water; on dry land you have a chance.
Sift the spreading puddle before it soaks into the ground.

monsters.name: Azer
monsters.blurb: Bronze-skinned dwarf-like smiths of the fire plane whose bodies are literally forges.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. Pry the chest plates apart carefully: a spilled core scorches for 1d6 fire.
Let it cool for an hour first, or it deforms under the knife.
Store in a metal tin; it sets cloth pouches alight.

monsters.name: Djinni
monsters.blurb: A towering, blue-skinned noble of the wind; its body dissolves into a warm breeze moments after death.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. Fail by 5 or more and the core bursts in a thunderclap (3d6 thunder).
Forms where the last breath left the body; search the air itself — it may be drifting.
Cut before the body dissolves (within 1 minute) and bind immediately or it floats away.

monsters.name: Efreeti
monsters.blurb: A cruel fire genie of brass and smoke; its corpse collapses into cinders and a single blazing heart-coal.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. The core is hot enough to melt steel tongs (2d6 fire on a failed check).
Sweep with a brass or stone tool; iron scoops fuse to the cinders.
Collect in crystal or clay; glass vials crack from the heat.

monsters.name: Dust Mephit
monsters.blurb: A sneezing, spiteful little imp of grit that explodes into a blinding cloud when killed.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. Its death-burst blinds whoever is closest; harvest with eyes shut and a steady hand (disadvantage unless blindfolded).

monsters.name: Ice Mephit
monsters.blurb: A cold, cruel little flier that shatters into shards when it dies.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. The shatter can cut you (1d4 slashing on a failed check).
Pack in snow or salt; they melt away in warm weather.

monsters.name: Magma Mephit
monsters.blurb: A lazy, dripping sprite of lava that bursts in a spatter of molten rock on death.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. Its death-burst sprays lava (1d6 fire to whoever reaches in first).

monsters.name: Steam Mephit
monsters.blurb: A hissing, sarcastic puff of steam that dies in a scalding burst.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. The burst scalds (1d4 fire) anyone harvesting without gloves.
Condense the dissipating steam on a cold blade.

monsters.name: Gargoyle
monsters.blurb: A spiteful, winged stone predator that poses as a carving until prey walks beneath it.

harvest.note: Requires a mason's chisel as well as a knife; hacking it apart leaves only gravel.
It looks like the rest of the rubble — detect magic or a DC 12 Investigation check helps find it.

monsters.name: Invisible Stalker
monsters.blurb: A bound air spirit that hunts a single target relentlessly and cannot be seen even in death.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. You cannot see it: work by touch and cold spots (disadvantage without see invisibility).
Found only by touch where the body collapsed; drop it and you may never find it again.

monsters.name: Magmin
monsters.blurb: A giggling little lump of living magma that detonates in flame when slain.

harvest.note: The mote unravels back into its element within 1 minute; seal it in an Essence Vessel before then. It explodes as it dies (1d6 fire in 10 feet); only the core survives the blast.

monsters.name: Salamander
monsters.blurb: A serpentine fire-noble whose body is so hot that metal glows near it.

harvest.note: Wait for the body to stop glowing or suffer 2d6 fire; carry it in a clay crucible.
Cut the tail in one sweep; it keeps constricting for an hour afterward.

monsters.name: Xorn
monsters.blurb: A three-armed, three-eyed mouth on legs that swims through rock and eats precious metals and gems.

harvest.note: Open the gizzard carefully; its grinding muscles keep working and can crush fingers.
If it is damaged, the phasing effect fails and it is just tripe.
It unravels back into its element within a minute. Seal it in an Essence Vessel before then.

monsters.name: Ghast
monsters.blurb: A ghoul-lord whose stench alone buckles the knees; its gear is ruin but its glands are prized.

harvest.note: Rupture it (fail by 5+) and you are poisoned for 1 hour.
Nick yourself (fail by 5+) and make a Con save or be paralysed for 1 minute.

monsters.name: Ghost
monsters.blurb: A lingering spirit bound to unfinished business; its ectoplasm must be caught as it discorporates.

harvest.note: Draw it into a silver-lined jar; ordinary glass lets it slip into the Ethereal.

It clings to the remains as a chill mist. Seal it in an Essence Vessel within a minute, before it seeps into the ground. A ghost that was merely 'destroyed' without being laid to rest yields a weaker, flickering essence (halve the value).
Found only by researching the ghost's life; taking it without resolving its business may invite a haunting.

monsters.name: Ghoul
monsters.blurb: A starving corpse-eater that paralyses its prey with filthy claws.

harvest.note: Scratch yourself (fail by 5+) and make a Con save or be paralysed for 1 minute.
Collect from the gums before it dries into useless crust.

monsters.name: Lich
monsters.blurb: An undying archmage who hid its soul in a phylactery; true harvest is only possible once that vessel is broken.

harvest.note: Only obtainable if the phylactery itself is destroyed; while it survives, shards are inert glass and the lich re-forms in days.
It clings to the remains as a chill mist. Seal it in an Essence Vessel within a minute, before it seeps into the ground. Only if the phylactery is gone; otherwise the essence flees to it.
Collect with a silver spoon; bare skin contact deals 2d6 necrotic.
Cold enough to cause frostbite (Con save or 1 level of exhaustion) without warded gloves.

monsters.name: Skeleton
monsters.blurb: Animated bones held together by necromancy; when it falls, the binding magic lingers in the marrow.

harvest.note: Grind it within a day of the skeleton's destruction or the necromantic charge fades.

monsters.name: Minotaur Skeleton
monsters.blurb: The reanimated bones of a minotaur, still charging mindlessly through old labyrinths.

harvest.note: Most skulls crack in the fight; only an intact one keeps its sense of direction.

monsters.name: Warhorse Skeleton
monsters.blurb: The bones of a fallen war mount, still charging for a long-dead rider.

monsters.name: Mummy
monsters.blurb: A preserved corpse animated by dark funerary rites, whose touch rots the flesh.

harvest.note: Touching bare skin risks mummy rot (DC 12 Con save). Keep away from flame — they burn like tinder.
Blindfold it the moment it is out; meeting its gaze can still frighten.

monsters.name: Mummy Lord
monsters.blurb: A god-blessed ruler raised by dark priests; destroy its heart or it will rise again.

harvest.note: The heart lies in a canopic jar in the tomb, not in the body. Taking it intact prevents the lord's return — as long as it is never 'fed'.
Mummy rot is far worse here (DC 16 Con save on contact).
Work fast and in darkness: light scatters it. An Essence Vessel holds it once sealed. Only possible if the heart has been taken or destroyed first.

monsters.name: Zombie
monsters.blurb: A shambling corpse that keeps standing up long after it should stay down.

harvest.note: Salt it heavily or it rots to slurry overnight.
Cut the sinews only after the head is destroyed, or the corpse may lurch back up.

monsters.name: Ogre Zombie
monsters.blurb: A rotting ogre corpse swinging a club with undead persistence.

harvest.note: Pry the club from the dead fingers; the grip is locked tight even after the zombie falls.

monsters.name: Shadow
monsters.blurb: A hungry scrap of darkness that saps strength with its touch.

harvest.note: Requires an Essence Vessel within 1 minute of death. It vanishes instantly in bright light; harvest in dim light only.
Scrape it up before dawn; sunlight burns it away.

monsters.name: Specter
monsters.blurb: A spiteful spirit that drains the life of anything warm.

harvest.note: Seal in a silver-lined vessel or it seeps away.
It clings to the remains as a chill mist. Seal it in an Essence Vessel within a minute, before it seeps into the ground.

monsters.name: Vampire
monsters.blurb: An ancient, aristocratic predator of blood; unless its heart is staked and burned, it simply rises in its coffin again.

harvest.note: Pull them from the skull within an hour of final death, before they crumble.
The vampire must be reduced to its coffin, its heart staked, and then burned in fire or sunlight. Without all three steps there is no ash — only a vampire that returns.
Collect before sunlight touches the body; exposure boils it away.
It clings to the remains as a chill mist. Seal it in an Essence Vessel within a minute, before it seeps into the ground. Only possible during the final destruction in the coffin.
Requires finding the resting place; the soil loses its potency once the vampire is truly dead for a week.

monsters.name: Vampire Spawn
monsters.blurb: A lesser vampire enslaved to its maker, hungry and wall-crawling.

harvest.note: Drain it in darkness; daylight boils it away.

monsters.name: Wight
monsters.blurb: A malevolent barrow-lord that drains life and raises its victims as zombies.

harvest.note: It clings to the remains as a chill mist. Seal it in an Essence Vessel within a minute, before it seeps into the ground.
Handling it bare-handed deals 1 necrotic damage per hour.

monsters.name: Will-o'-Wisp
monsters.blurb: A malicious ball of light that lures travellers into bogs and feeds on their final breaths.

harvest.note: It clings to the remains as a chill mist. Seal it in an Essence Vessel within a minute, before it seeps into the ground. It turns invisible as it fades; a failed check costs 1d8 lightning damage.
Skim it off the water's surface with a flat blade.

monsters.name: Wraith
monsters.blurb: A hateful spirit of darkness that drains life and turns its victims into specters.

harvest.note: Seal in silver; it drifts through lead and glass alike.
Work fast and in darkness: light scatters it. An Essence Vessel holds it once sealed. A failed check drains 1d8 from your hit point maximum until a long rest.

monsters.name: Animated Armor
monsters.blurb: An empty suit of plate that guards a vault or hall until knocked apart.

harvest.note: Usually inside the breastplate; pry it out gently or the rune cracks and goes dark.

monsters.name: Clay Golem
monsters.blurb: A holy guardian sculpted from clay; its blows leave wounds that magic can barely heal.

harvest.note: Must be removed intact from inside the head; breaking it destroys the binding script.
Keep it wet; clay that dries out loses its curse.

monsters.name: Flesh Golem
monsters.blurb: A stitched-together giant of corpse-parts driven by a bound spirit and bottled lightning.

harvest.note: Still charged: fail and take 2d6 lightning damage.
Cut along the seams, never across them.

monsters.name: Flying Sword
monsters.blurb: A longsword animated to dance through the air and guard its master's halls.

harvest.note: Knocked-apart swords are often bent; roll to see if the blade is salvageable.

monsters.name: Homunculus
monsters.blurb: A tiny winged servant grown from clay, ash and a wizard's blood, bound telepathically to its maker.

harvest.note: Killing a homunculus alerts its creator, who feels the link break.
Prick yourself (fail by 5+) and make a Con save or fall unconscious for 1 hour.

monsters.name: Iron Golem
monsters.blurb: A colossal iron guardian that breathes poison and heals in fire.

harvest.note: Buried behind the chest plates; cutting through takes 8 hours with smith's tools.
Opening the vent releases a last puff of poison (DC 15 Con save or 4d8 poison).
Needs a forge on site or heavy transport; each plate weighs 100 lb.

monsters.name: Rug of Smothering
monsters.blurb: A fine carpet that lies in wait, then wraps and suffocates intruders.

harvest.note: Unpick the intact portion; slashed sections lose their grip.

monsters.name: Shield Guardian
monsters.blurb: A bodyguard construct bound to an amulet; it shields its master and can store a spell.

harvest.note: Only if the control amulet is captured or broken; the shard is taken from it, not the body.
If a spell is still stored, it may trigger when the cavity is cut free.

monsters.name: Stone Golem
monsters.blurb: A massive carved guardian that can make intruders slow and sluggish.

harvest.note: Requires masons' tools; 4 hours of chiselling to reach the core.
Only the stones around the carved eyes carry the slowing power.

monsters.name: Black Pudding
monsters.blurb: A heaving mass of black acid that splits in two when cut and dissolves weapons that strike it.

harvest.note: Only glass, stone or crystal vials hold it; metal tools dissolve (lose any metal implement on a fail).
Must be cut while the ooze still quivers.

monsters.name: Gelatinous Cube
monsters.blurb: A nearly invisible dungeon-cleaning cube that engulfs everything it rolls over.

harvest.note: Gloves required; bare skin takes 1d6 acid per minute of contact.
Roll on your GM's treasure table; organics are usually half-digested.

monsters.name: Gray Ooze
monsters.blurb: A puddle of slime that looks like wet stone and eats metal.

harvest.note: Metal tools corrode; use wood or bone scrapers.
Only forms if you let a sample dry in the sun for a day.

monsters.name: Ochre Jelly
monsters.blurb: A yellow, acidic blob that splits when struck with lightning or blades.

harvest.note: Must be cut while it still quivers.

monsters.name: Awakened Shrub
monsters.blurb: A bush granted awareness by druidic magic.

harvest.note: Pluck from living branches; leaves from a burned shrub are silent.

monsters.name: Awakened Tree
monsters.blurb: A tree granted speech and movement by druidic magic.

harvest.note: Tap it within a day of the tree's death.
Requires an axe and 2 hours of work.

monsters.name: Shambling Mound
monsters.blurb: A heap of rotting vegetation that engulfs prey and grows stronger when struck by lightning.

harvest.note: Still carry charge: fail by 5+ and take 2d6 lightning.
Dig through the engulfing muck to find it; smells horrendous.

monsters.name: Shrieker
monsters.blurb: A giant mushroom that screams when light or movement disturbs it.

harvest.note: Picking it sets off one final shriek — nearby creatures will come to investigate.

monsters.name: Treant
monsters.blurb: An ancient guardian of the forest that can awaken trees to fight beside it.

harvest.note: Harvesting heartwood from a treant draws the ire of the forest's guardians unless a druid performs a rite.
A faint shimmer over the body marks it. Catch it in an Essence Vessel within a minute.
Only 1 in 4 treants carries a seed-acorn.

monsters.name: Violet Fungus
monsters.blurb: A purple mushroom that lashes with rotting tendrils.

harvest.note: Contact causes 1d4 necrotic damage without gloves.
